answer.generated: Real-time systems require specific timing design because they must meet strict deadlines, whereas general information systems typically do not. Unlike non-real-time systems, real-time systems often lack database design, as timing constraints take precedence over data management. The architectural design for real-time systems must account for these timing requirements, focusing on how components interact under tight time constraints, unlike the more flexible approach in conventional systems.
